ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a world map, marking the locations of four earthquakes above magnitude seven from January to February 2013, ①②③④, and using small boxes beside them to label the magnitude and focal depth. ① is located near the interior of Asia, labeled with a magnitude of about 7.3 and a focal depth of 10 kilometers; ② is located near the west coast of North America, labeled with a magnitude of about 7.8 and a focal depth of 10 kilometers; ③ is located near western South America, labeled with a magnitude of about 7.0 and a focal depth of 130 kilometers; ④ is located on the northeast side of Australia, near the Southwest Pacific Ocean area, labeled with a magnitude of about 7.5 and a focal depth of 10 kilometers. The legend explains that black dots are epicenter locations, and the number boxes indicate magnitude and focal depth. Then reason: Tsunamis are usually triggered by earthquakes that occur in sea areas or near-shore seabeds, have shallow focal depths, and have large magnitudes. ① is inland, so it does not fit; ③ has a relatively deep focal depth, so it is not very likely to trigger a tsunami; although ② is close to the coast, ④ is more obviously located in the Southwest Pacific Ocean area and has a shallow focus and large magnitude, best fitting the conditions for triggering a tsunami. Therefore the answer is place ④.
